newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi has device to cut diesel emissions.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi has device to cut diesel emissions.

text.p: Mitsubishi Motors Corp said on Tuesday it has developed a system to eliminate 80 percent of the particle emissions from diesel engines.
The system called "Mitsubishi DPF" consists of a ceramic filter for retrieving particulate matter and a heater for burning up the retrieved particles.

The system will reduce emissions of particulate to 0.125 gram/kilowatt hour (kwh), sharply lower than Japan's long-term regulation, effective October 1998, which sets a limit of 0.25 gram/kwh. The system can eliminate virtually 100 percent of the black smoke emitted from diesel engines.
The system does not clear the Japan's targeted nitrogen oxide (NOx) emission requirement of 4.5 gram/kwh.
The system will cost roughly 4.5 million yen for each unit. Mitsubishi will supply 30 systems for installation in Yokohama city's buses by the end of March 1997.
